html:
In April 1988 Kanak independence activists attacked a gendarmerie on the island of Ouvéa, killing four gendarmes and taking others hostage to a cave. On 5 May French troops stormed the cave; 19 Kanak and two soldiers died.

It came at the peak of the years called the Events, between France's state and the Kanak movement, and between the first round and the runoff of the French presidential election.

Evidence that some captives were killed after the assault caused outrage. The shock pushed both sides to sign the Matignon Accords that June, led by Jean-Marie Tjibaou, and later the Nouméa Accord. Tjibaou himself was killed on Ouvéa a year later.
